analysis.title: "Enjoy The GPUphoria While It Lasts": Why Bernstein And HSBC Still Say Sell After CoreWeave's Best Quarter Ever
key_insights: CoreWeave Q3 beat: revenue $3.66B, margins beat, full-year guide raised, backlog $132.5B. Stock up over 20% to near $60 in early trading, Nvidia up 3%. The euro bond rose as much as 3.6 cents to 79.8.

Bernstein (Madison Rezaei) kept Underperform and a $54 target (22.5x forward adjusted EBIT, trimmed from 23.5x) after calling it about the best quarter it could have asked for. Near-term floor is $45-$54, with upside of $64-$73 if AI sentiment turns. It views October's de-rating as semi-permanent, against a six-month average multiple of 27x.

HSBC (Abhishek Shukla) kept Reduce and a $39 target, about 30% below the current price. Neither bear disputes the quarter. Both object to what it is being used to prove: an unverifiable price point, a roughly $33B funding gap for next year, and a supply wave far larger than CoreWeave.

Bernstein's first leap of faith is that data center supply stays tight. Bernstein expects about 55GW of announced capacity through 2028 across clouds, neoclouds and SpaceX (75GW before haircut), with CoreWeave's share at 2-3GW. CoreWeave is holding back 2028 capacity to wait for higher pricing (referencing $40M/MW).

Management said over 130,000 GPUs come off contract in 2027 and about 170,000 more in 2028, and that re-renting them would generate nearly $4B and nearly $10B of annualized revenue. Bernstein backs out an implied $3.81 per GPU-hour, or $24M per MW per year, for 3-5 year old chips. At $2.00/hr (Silicon Data H100 index, last December) the $10B becomes $5.3B, and at $1.70 (SemiAnalysis October 2025 trough) it becomes $4.5B.

HSBC tested the claim of $20-25M per MW per year on 4-5 year contracts, and up to $40M short-term, after a 25% price hike in July and another 10% later in the quarter. It estimates historical realized pricing at $12-13M per MW. Bernstein's calculation (reported revenue over average active power) gives $9.2M in Q3, below $10.7M two years ago. Goldman's own worked example ($11B per year per GW) is $11M per MW.

HSBC uses asset turnover as the test: 30.5% in Q3 vs 28.6% in Q2, 30.0% in 2025 and 34.8% in 2024. The raised $21B exit run-rate against Q4 capex implies about 32.6%, in line with the 33% HSBC models and near Oracle's cloud business. HSBC's rule of thumb is about $50B all-in per GW ($37.5B of IT gear plus $12.5B of leased shell), so 33% turnover gives about $12.4M per MW.

The 10.4% adjusted operating margin compares with guidance of 6.5%, but the company averaged about 16% before the recent dip and talks about 25% long term. HSBC says estimates were anchored on sandbagged guidance. The 2027 guide of EBITDA over interest expense (excluding prepayments) rising more than 2x compares with consensus and HSBC already at 2.4x-2.6x.

The backlog is lengthening, not shortening toward short-term deals. In Q2, 41% of the $103.7B backlog was due within 24 months. In Q3 the share was 36% of $132.5B. Goldman's Borges says 95%+ of the business is 4-5 year take-or-pay, so $40M spot pricing is a small part of the mix.

Funding gap: Bernstein puts it at $32.5B against about $60B of backlog delivery cost. HSBC estimates $33B of new financing needed in 2027, with undrawn credit lines down to $5B from $10B in a quarter. Management cites $6.5B cash and securities ($4.2B unrestricted), nearly $5B undrawn DDTLs, about $9B customer prepayments within three months, and under $5B of new parent-level capital needed through 2027.

The funding plan depends on lenders and customers. The next DDTL is expected to be investment grade at 7.0%-7.5% and fund over 90% of capex, which thins the equity cushion. Customer prepayments now run 15%-50% of contract value versus 15%-25% at end of 2025 (Bernstein), and probably carry interest. CoreWeave sold $4.2B of converts in the quarter and filed an ATM for up to 35M shares, which Bernstein sees costing the stock 2%-6%.

Balance sheet and coverage: Q3 interest of $846M was over 2x adjusted operating income. Debt rose $11.8B in a quarter to $46.9B against $4.0B of equity. Net debt to EBITDA is 7.3x. Bernstein sees 3Q27 adjusted operating income of $1.02B against $1.56B of interest. Adjusted net income does not turn positive until 1H28. Operating lease liabilities were $18.7B at end of September, up from $8.2B at year-end.

HSBC sees free cash flow negative every year through 2030 (about $74B cumulative burn from 2026), with net debt rising from $38B at end of this year to $96B. Goldman's base case has capex at steady state in 2028 and FCF positive in 2030. HSBC raised 2028-2030 revenue, EBITDA and operating profit but cut 2028 EPS 15% to $0.82 from $0.96, because higher capex (2028 up 27%) lifts interest expense 14%-20%.

The two bears differ in their models. HSBC has a profit in 2028 and EPS of $2.58 in 2029, and still finds the stock expensive at 11.7x 2030 EV/EBIT after stock comp against 6.6x for Oracle. Bernstein has losses widening to $8.09 per share in 2029. Bernstein raised its 2026 adjusted EPS loss estimate to $3.54 from $5.14 and its 2027 loss to $3.20 from $6.60.

Goldman's Gabriela Borges (Buy since Oct 19) describes the DDTL funding structure: an SPV with about 80% debt and 20% equity, drawn in stages, repaid by customer payments, with residual GPU value accruing to CoreWeave. In her example, $11B a year over four years ($44B) needs about 1GW at $37.5B capex. She attributes the CDS widening to its being a liquid hedge for data center exposure, and says the $10B of unsecured parent debt at a 16% yield to worst does not reflect secured financing costs.

Other skeptics: D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria says interest expense far exceeds adjusted operating income. MoffettNathanson's Nick Del Deo flagged Texas policy risk and the 16% parent yield. UBS's Karl Keirstead sees confidence taking several quarters to rebuild. Stifel trimmed its target citing funding. Chamath Palihapitiya in Goldman's Top of Mind puts breakeven utilization at roughly 70%-75%, and calls neoclouds that lease shells middlemen.

The author notes Goldman is at the top of the syndicate for Anthropic's $100B IPO, being marketed this week. The author sides with the bears on the three-year view and with the tape for as long as the rally lasts. The next test is the investment-grade DDTL, expected to price at 7.0%-7.5% within weeks.

market_movers.rationale: Bernstein concedes the quarter but sees supply of about 55GW through 2028 pressuring pricing, a roughly $32.5B funding gap and interest exceeding operating income. Raised estimates but cut the target multiple to 22.5x forward adjusted EBIT.
HSBC sees asset turnover of about 30.5% not supporting claimed doubled pricing, a $33B financing need in 2027 and negative FCF through 2030. Cut 2028 EPS 15% on higher interest costs.
Goldman's Gabriela Borges upgraded on Oct 19 and defends the DDTL funding model, with capex reaching steady state in 2028 and FCF positive in 2030.
Stifel trimmed its target citing funding concerns. UBS's Keirstead says rebuilding confidence takes several quarters.

sector_views.rationale: Bears see about 55GW of new supply through 2028 pressuring GPU rental prices, leveraged balance sheets and funding that depends on lenders and customer prepayments. The author cites Gartner expecting more than 80% of neoclouds to fold.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave Q3 2026 reported revenue $3.66B (beat). Adjusted operating margin 10.4% reported vs company guidance of 6.5%. Full-year guide raised, backlog $132.5B vs $103.7B in Q2.
CoreWeave Q3 interest expense $846M, more than 2x adjusted operating income. Debt $46.9B (up $11.8B in the quarter), equity $4.0B. Net debt to EBITDA 7.3x.

Bernstein estimates: 2026 adjusted EPS loss of $3.54 (previously loss of $5.14), 2027 loss of $3.20 (previously loss of $6.60), 2029 loss of $8.09. 3Q27 adjusted operating income $1.02B vs interest $1.56B.
HSBC estimates: 2028 EPS $0.82 (cut 15% from $0.96), 2029 EPS $2.58. FCF negative through 2030, about $74B cumulative burn from 2026. Net debt $38B at end 2026, rising to $96B.
2027 guide: EBITDA over interest expense, excluding prepayments, to rise more than 2x. Consensus and HSBC estimates were already 2.4x-2.6x.
Asset turnover (revenue per dollar of installed equipment): 30.5% in Q3, 28.6% in Q2, 30.0% in 2025, 34.8% in 2024. Guidance implies about 32.6%.
CoreWeave sold $4.2B of converts in the quarter and filed an ATM for up to 35M shares.
risk_factors: Supply wave: about 55GW (75GW before haircut) of announced capacity through 2028 could cut compute prices (Bernstein, Goldman's Borges acknowledges the same risk).
Funding gap of about $32.5B-$33B in 2027, dependent on new DDTLs at 7.0%-7.5% and customer prepayments.
Collateral risk: GPU resale value and obsolescence on long-dated commitments to one GPU generation.
Interest expense exceeds adjusted operating income, and adjusted net income does not turn positive until 1H28 (Bernstein).
Utilization risk: breakeven utilization of roughly 70%-75%, with the 75%-85% range described as a gray zone (Palihapitiya).
Equity dilution from the ATM for up to 35M shares and converts.
Texas policy risk and physical delivery of the backlog.
vol_and_positioning: CoreWeave euro bond rose as much as 3.6 cents to 79.8, its largest move since July. The parent's $10B unsecured debt trades at a 16% yield to worst. CoreWeave CDS is widely used as a hedge for data center exposure because it is one of the few liquid data center swaps (per Goldman).

CoreWeave stock was down 65% from its May high before the print, and rose over 20% to near $60 after it. Bernstein says the October de-rating is semi-permanent, with the six-month average multiple at 27x.
Bernstein estimates ATM usage would cost the stock 2%-6%.
geopolitical: Texas governor-elect wants a pause on data center development (flagged by MoffettNathanson as policy risk for CoreWeave).
cross_bank_references: Bernstein and HSBC both keep sell-equivalent ratings after the Q3 print and independently size the 2027 funding gap at about $33B.
Goldman's Gabriela Borges (Buy) names supply as a key risk, the same variable Bernstein builds its Underperform on.
HSBC's $11.8M-per-MW-type test is set against Goldman's worked example of $11B a year per GW ($11M per MW).

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Borges argues the DDTL structure funds contracts mostly with customer-credit-rated secured debt, repaid inside the contract term. Capex reaches steady state in 2028 and FCF turns positive in 2030. Management says pricing is $20-25M per MW with a next DDTL at 7.0%-7.5%.
tension_points.bear_case: Bernstein and HSBC see a roughly $33B funding gap, about 55GW of new supply through 2028 pressuring prices, interest expense above adjusted operating income and negative FCF through 2030. Realized pricing of $9-13M per MW does not show the claimed doubling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The next investment-grade DDTL failing to price at 7.0%-7.5% within weeks would undercut the bull case. Sustained GPU rental pricing above $2.00 per hour would undermine the bears' re-rental math.

theme_stances.key_argument: Bernstein and HSBC see a roughly $33B funding gap and a supply wave that pressures GPU pricing and collateral value.
Goldman's Borges argues secured DDTLs price far below the parent debt yield and that capex reaches steady state in 2028.
